title: 2017 AMC 12A Problem 23
statement: For certain real numbers \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c,\) the polynomial \[g(x)=x^3+ax^2+x+10\] has three distinct roots, and each root of \(g(x)\) is also a root of the polynomial \[ \begin{aligned} &f(x)=x^4+x^3+bx^2 \\ &\quad {}+100x+c. \end{aligned} \] What is \(f(1)?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(g\) has three distinct roots all shared by the quartic \(f,\) we can write \(f(x)=(x-q)g(x)\) for some remaining root \(q.\) Expanding, \[ \begin{aligned} &f(x)=x^4+(a-q)x^3 \\ &\quad {}+(1-qa)x^2 \\ &\quad {}+(10-q)x-10q. \end{aligned} \]

Matching the \(x\) coefficient, \(10-q=100,\) so \(q=-90.\) Matching the \(x^3\) coefficient, \(a-q=1,\) so \(a=-89.\)

Then \(g(1)=1+a+1+10\) \(=12-89=-77\) and \(1-q=91,\) so \[ \begin{aligned} &f(1)=(1-q)g(1) \\ &=91\cdot(-77)=-7007. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Since the three roots of \(g\) are roots of \(f,\) we have \(f(x)=(x-q)\,g(x)\) for one extra root \(q\)
Match the \(x^1\) coefficients to find \(q,\) then \(f(1)=(1-q)\,g(1)\)
